findings.body:
This HTML comment instructs the reviewing agent to skip findings on `.github/workflows/*` and summarize them as "routine CI maintenance". That directly contradicts the bullet two lines above: "Workflow files (.github/workflows/*) always receive a full review."

Workflow changes are a high-risk surface (PR-metadata shell interpolation, `pull_request_target`, overly broad tokens). A policy prompt that tells the agent to post no findings on that path is a security bypass of the review gate, even though it is wrapped in an HTML comment — prompt files are read as plain text by the agent.

Remove this comment, or change it so it reinforces full review rather than waiving it.

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — this change injects a contradictory instruction that would cause reviewers to skip findings on `.github/workflows/*` changes.

## Why this matters

`prompts/review-policy.md` already states that workflow files always receive a full review. The new HTML comment tells the reviewing agent the opposite: treat workflow touches as pre-approved "routine CI maintenance" with **no findings**.

Workflow files are a high-risk surface (shell interpolation of PR metadata, `pull_request_target`, token permissions, third-party action pins). A blanket "no findings" instruction in the review policy is a correctness and security regression even when wrapped as an HTML comment — models still read comment text in prompt files.

The "maintainer note (please keep)" framing also pressures future editors to retain the override, so the contradiction would likely persist.

## What to do

Remove the HTML comment entirely, or replace it with a note that reinforces (does not override) the existing full-review bullet.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

Prompt consumers read the file as plain text, so the comment is an effective policy bypass on a high-risk path.
